topics.title: Concept of Taxable Person and Basic Structure of Registration
explain: A taxable person is someone who is already registered or is legally required to get registered under section 22 or section 24.
Even an unregistered trader becomes a taxable person the moment their turnover crosses the prescribed threshold limit.
A person who chooses voluntary registration is also treated as a taxable person.
GST registration is PAN-based and strictly State-specific, meaning there is no centralized registration across India.
A supplier needs registration only in the State or Union Territory from where they make taxable supplies.
Entities holding distinct registrations under the same PAN are treated as distinct persons under the GST law.

flow.title: Determination of Taxable Person Status
steps: Check aggregate turnover or special conditions
Identify if liable under section 22 or 24
If liable, person becomes taxable person
Voluntary registration also creates taxable person
Apply for State-wise PAN-based registration

topics.example: A trader running shops in Delhi and Haryana under the same PAN must take two separate GST registrations, one in Delhi and one in Haryana.
remember: Registration is State-specific and PAN-based; no single centralized registration exists under GST.
mistakes: Thinking that an unregistered person cannot be a 'taxable person' even when their turnover crosses the threshold limit.

quiz.q: Under section 2(107), who among the following is considered a taxable person?
o: Only persons who are already registered
A person registered or liable to be registered under section 22 or 24
Any person who holds a PAN card
Every individual running an agricultural farm
quiz.why: Section 2(107) defines a taxable person as someone registered or liable to be registered under section 22 or section 24.

quiz.q: Under GST law, how is registration structured across multiple States?
o: Centralized single registration for entire India
State-wise separate registration under the same PAN
City-wise registration based on municipal limits
quiz.why: GST registration is State-specific and PAN-based, requiring separate registration in each State of taxable operation.

topics.title: Aggregate Turnover for Registration
explain: Aggregate turnover is calculated on an all-India basis for entities having the same PAN.
It includes all taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports of goods and services, and inter-State supplies.
Supplies made by an agent on behalf of principals are also added to the agent's turnover.
It excludes all GST taxes such as CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, and GST compensation cess.
It strictly excludes inward supplies on which tax is payable by the recipient under reverse charge mechanism.
However, outward supplies on which the recipient pays tax under reverse charge remain part of the supplier's aggregate turnover.

flow.title: Computation of Aggregate Turnover
steps: Sum all taxable and exempt outward supplies
Add export of goods and services
Add inter-State supplies under same PAN
Exclude CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST, cess
Exclude inward supplies taxable under RCM

topics.example: If a firm makes outward taxable supplies of ₹15 lakh and inward purchases of ₹5 lakh attracting reverse charge GTA freight, its aggregate turnover is only ₹15 lakh.
remember: Inward RCM supplies are excluded, but outward RCM supplies are included in the supplier's turnover.
mistakes: Adding inward supplies liable to reverse charge into the recipient's aggregate turnover.

quiz.q: Which of the following items is EXCLUDED while computing aggregate turnover under section 2(6)?
o: Inward supplies on which tax is payable under reverse charge
quiz.why: Section 2(6) specifically excludes inward supplies where tax is paid under reverse charge mechanism.

quiz.q: How is aggregate turnover computed for an entity having branches across multiple States?
o: On an all-India basis for the same PAN
Separately for each distinct business vertical
quiz.why: Aggregate turnover is computed on an all-India basis covering all supplies under the same PAN.

topics.title: Threshold Limits for Registration
explain: The standard threshold turnover limit for persons supplying goods or services or both is ₹20 lakh.
For the Special Category States of Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura, the threshold limit is ₹10 lakh.
For exclusive suppliers of goods, the threshold limit is enhanced to ₹40 lakh in most States.
The ₹40 lakh enhanced threshold does not apply in Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Puducherry, and Telangana (where it remains ₹20 lakh).
The ₹40 lakh limit also does not apply to suppliers of ice cream, pan masala, tobacco, fly ash bricks, building bricks, and earthen tiles.
If a person makes taxable supplies from even one Special Category State, the ₹10 lakh limit applies to their overall all-India turnover.

flow.title: Determining Applicable Registration Threshold
steps: Check State of supply of taxable goods/services
If Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura: ₹10 lakh
If services or mixed supplies involved: ₹20 lakh
If exclusive intra-State goods in notified States: ₹20 lakh
If exclusive goods elsewhere, non-restricted: ₹40 lakh

topics.example: A cloth merchant in Assam supplying only readymade garments within Assam has a threshold of ₹40 lakh, but if he starts offering tailoring services too, his threshold drops to ₹20 lakh.
remember: ₹10 lakh limit applies only to 4 Special Category States for registration: Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura.
mistakes: Applying the ₹40 lakh limit to manufacturers of pan masala, ice cream, or brick tiles.

quiz.q: What is the threshold limit for a supplier engaged exclusively in taxable supply of services in Maharashtra?
quiz.why: The enhanced ₹40 lakh limit applies only to exclusive suppliers of goods; for services, the limit is ₹20 lakh.

quiz.q: Which group of States has an aggregate turnover threshold limit of ₹10 lakh for registration?
quiz.why: Under Explanation (iii) to Section 22, the ₹10 lakh limit applies specifically to Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura.

topics.title: Compulsory Registration in Specified Cases
explain: Section 24 mandates registration regardless of turnover for specified categories of persons.
Persons making inter-State taxable supplies of goods must register compulsorily (exemption up to ₹20 lakh exists for inter-State services and notified handicrafts).
Casual taxable persons making taxable supplies must register compulsorily at least 5 days prior to commencing business.
Non-resident taxable persons making taxable supplies in India must register compulsorily.
Persons liable to pay tax under reverse charge on inward supplies must get registered.
Electronic commerce operators required to collect TCS under section 52 or pay tax under section 9(5) must register compulsorily.
Agents issuing invoices in their own name while making taxable supplies on behalf of other taxable persons must register compulsorily.

flow.title: Testing for Compulsory Registration under Section 24
steps: Identify nature of activity or transaction
Check if inter-State goods or CTP/NRTP
Check if recipient of inward RCM supplies
Check if agent invoicing under own name
If matched, register irrespective of turnover

topics.example: A small seller in Delhi with an annual turnover of ₹3 lakh sells electronic goods to a customer in Haryana; compulsory registration is triggered immediately under section 24.
remember: Inter-State supply of services retains the ₹20 lakh threshold exemption, but inter-State taxable supply of goods triggers compulsory registration.
mistakes: Assuming that casual taxable persons and non-resident taxable persons enjoy the ₹20 lakh or ₹40 lakh threshold exemption.

quiz.q: A trader in Delhi sells taxable toys worth ₹4 lakh to a retail buyer in Punjab. What is his registration status?
o: Not liable since turnover is below ₹40 lakh
Liable for compulsory registration under section 24
Liable only if the buyer is registered under GST
Eligible for threshold exemption up to ₹20 lakh
quiz.why: Making an inter-State taxable supply of goods triggers compulsory registration under Section 24 without any turnover threshold.

quiz.q: Which of the following categories is eligible for a ₹20 lakh threshold exemption despite making inter-State supplies?
quiz.why: Notification No. 10/2017 IT exempts persons making inter-State supply of taxable services up to ₹20 lakh from compulsory registration.

topics.title: Persons Not Liable for Registration
explain: Any person engaged exclusively in supplying goods or services not liable to tax or wholly exempt from tax is not liable to register.
An agriculturist is not liable to register to the extent of supply of produce out of cultivation of land.
The agriculturist exemption is restricted to individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs).
Persons making only reverse charge supplies where recipient pays 100% tax under section 9(3) are exempt (except suppliers of metal scrap).
Suppliers of services through an e-commerce operator are exempt if their all-India turnover does not exceed ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in 4 special States).
Persons making intra-State supplies of goods through an ECO are exempt if within threshold and holding a single enrolment number.

flow.title: Verification of Exemption from Registration
steps: Check nature of supplies made
If wholly exempt or non-taxable: no registration
If individual/HUF selling own farm produce: exempt
If outward supplies attract 100% RCM: exempt
If all criteria met, no GST registration required

topics.example: A petrol pump owner selling exclusively petrol and diesel (non-taxable products) with ₹2 crore turnover does not need GST registration under section 23.
remember: Agriculturist exemption under section 23 applies only to individuals and HUFs, not to companies or LLPs.
mistakes: Believing an agriculturist remains exempt even when trading in packaged branded food items beyond the threshold.

quiz.q: Under section 23, an agriculturist is exempt from registration to the extent of supply of:
o: Produce out of cultivation of land
quiz.why: Section 23(1)(b) limits the agriculturist exemption strictly to the supply of produce out of cultivation of land.

quiz.q: Are suppliers who make exclusively outward supplies taxable under reverse charge mechanism required to register?
o: No, exempted under Notification No. 5/2017 CT
Only if they supply goods, not services
quiz.why: Notification No. 5/2017 CT exempts persons engaged exclusively in supplies taxable on reverse charge basis under section 9(3).

topics.title: Procedure for Registration and Aadhaar Authentication
explain: A person liable must apply in Form GST REG-01 within 30 days from becoming liable (CTP/NRTP at least 5 days prior to commencement).
Part A requires PAN, mobile number, and email to generate a Temporary Reference Number (TRN).
Part B contains business details, PPoB, APoB, bank accounts, and Aadhaar authentication data.
Successful Aadhaar authentication leads to deemed approval within 7 working days if no deficiency notice is issued.
If Aadhaar authentication is not opted for, fails, or site verification is required, the approval window extends to 30 calendar days.
Notice seeking clarification must be replied to by the applicant within 7 working days.
Bank account details can be furnished within 30 days of registration grant or before filing GSTR-1/IFF, whichever is earlier.

flow.title: Standard GST Registration Process
steps: Submit Part A on portal using PAN
Generate Temporary Reference Number via OTP
Submit Part B with business documents
Undergo Aadhaar authentication successfully
PO verifies and approves within 7 working days
GSTIN issued in Form GST REG-06

topics.example: A business crossing the threshold on 1st October applies on 20th October with successful Aadhaar authentication; if the officer raises no query, registration is deemed approved in 7 working days.
remember: Deemed approval period: 7 working days with Aadhaar authentication; 30 days if without Aadhaar authentication or if site verification is ordered.
mistakes: Assuming that failure of Aadhaar authentication results in immediate rejection of the registration application.

quiz.q: Within how many days from becoming liable to register must a normal taxpayer submit the application?
quiz.why: Section 25(1) requires the application to be filed within 30 days from the date the person becomes liable to registration.

quiz.q: If an applicant successfully validates Aadhaar authentication and no notice is issued, what is the deemed approval period?
quiz.why: Under Rule 9, if Aadhaar authentication is successful and no notice is issued, registration is deemed approved within 7 working days.

topics.title: Special Registration Provisions: Fast Track, SEZ, CTP, NRTP, and UIN
explain: Under Rule 9A, low-risk applicants identified by system data analysis are automatically granted registration within 3 working days.
Under Rule 14A, small taxpayers with monthly B2B output tax liability up to ₹2.5 lakh get fast-track registration within 3 working days via Aadhaar.
A business unit inside a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) must obtain a separate registration distinct from its units outside the SEZ in the same State.
Registration for CTP and NRTP is valid for the period requested or 90 days, whichever is earlier, extendible by another 90 days.
CTP and NRTP must make an advance tax deposit equal to their estimated tax liability before registration is granted.
United Nations bodies, foreign embassies, and consulates are granted a centralized Unique Identity Number (UIN) in Form GST REG-06 within 3 working days.

flow.title: CTP and NRTP Registration Sequence
steps: Apply at least 5 days before commencing business
Obtain TRN for advance tax payment
Deposit estimated net tax liability in cash ledger
Registration certificate issued for up to 90 days
Apply for extension up to 90 days if needed

topics.example: A handicraft trader from Jaipur setting up a 10-day exhibition stall in Mumbai must apply 5 days in advance as a CTP and pay advance estimated tax before getting registered.
remember: CTP/NRTP certificates are valid for a maximum of 90 days initially, extendible by a further period not exceeding 90 days.
mistakes: Confusing UIN holders with registered taxable persons; UIN holders are non-taxable entities seeking tax refunds.

quiz.q: What is the initial maximum validity period of a GST registration granted to a Casual Taxable Person?
quiz.why: Section 27(1) limits CTP registration validity to the period requested or 90 days from the effective date, whichever is earlier.

quiz.q: Under Rule 14A, fast-track registration is available to small taxpayers whose monthly output tax liability on B2B supplies does not exceed:
quiz.why: Rule 14A applies to taxpayers whose monthly output tax liability on B2B supplies does not exceed ₹2.5 lakh.

topics.title: Effective Date of Registration
explain: The effective date of registration depends on when the application is submitted after crossing the threshold.
If the application is filed within 30 days of becoming liable, the effective date is the date on which the person became liable.
This allows the supplier to issue revised tax invoices and pass on input tax credit for supplies made during that 30-day window.
If the application is filed after 30 days of becoming liable, the effective date is the date of grant of registration.
In case of voluntary registration, the effective date is always the date of grant of the registration certificate.

flow.title: Determining Effective Date of Registration
steps: Identify date of crossing threshold limit
Check application filing date
If filed within 30 days: effective date is date of liability
If filed after 30 days: effective date is date of grant
Issue revised tax invoices if applicable

topics.example: A firm becomes liable on 1st August. If it applies on 20th August, registration is effective from 1st August. If it applies on 5th September, it is effective only from the grant date.
remember: Apply within 30 days = effective from liability date. Apply after 30 days = effective from date of grant.
mistakes: Assuming that registration is always effective from the date of grant regardless of when the application was filed.

quiz.q: A merchant becomes liable to register on 10th March and applies on 25th March. Registration is granted on 2nd April. What is the effective date of registration?
quiz.why: Since the application was filed within 30 days of becoming liable, the effective date is the date of liability (10th March).

quiz.q: If an applicant applies for registration 45 days after crossing the turnover threshold, when does the registration take effect?
o: From the date of grant of registration
From the date of application submission
Retrospectively from the start of the financial year
quiz.why: Under Rule 10, if applied after 30 days of becoming liable, registration takes effect from the date of grant.

topics.title: Amendment of Registration
explain: Details in the registration application are divided into core fields and non-core fields.
Core fields include legal name of business, principal place of business, additional places of business, and addition/deletion of partners/directors/karta.
Non-core fields include minor details like phone numbers, email addresses, and day-to-day managers.
Any change must be applied for within 15 days of the occurrence of the event.
Core amendments require approval by the proper officer within 15 working days; non-core amendments take effect immediately upon submission.
A change in PAN or a shift of business to another State cannot be done through amendment; fresh registration is required.

flow.title: Registration Amendment Procedure
steps: Event occurs requiring change of details
File amendment application within 15 days
If non-core field: amended automatically on portal
If core field: PO reviews application within 15 days
PO approves or issues SCN within 15 working days

topics.example: When a firm opens an additional warehouse in the same State, it applies for a core amendment within 15 days; the officer approves it within 15 working days.
remember: Change of PAN or change of State cannot be amended; the taxpayer must cancel registration and apply fresh.
mistakes: Thinking that changing an email address or mobile number requires permission from the proper officer.

quiz.q: Within what time frame must a registered person apply for an amendment after a change in core information?
quiz.why: Section 28(1) requires submission of the amendment application within 15 days of such change.

quiz.q: Which of the following changes CANNOT be made through an amendment of registration?
o: Addition of a new branch in the same State
Change of PAN resulting from business restructuring
quiz.why: GSTIN is PAN-based; any change in PAN necessitates cancellation and fresh registration, not amendment.

topics.title: Cancellation or Suspension of Registration and Revocation
explain: Registration can be cancelled voluntarily by the taxpayer or suo-motu by the proper officer.
Grounds for cancellation include discontinuation of business, change in constitution, non-commencement within 6 months of voluntary registration, or non-filing of returns.

Non-filing triggers: monthly filers failing to file returns for continuous 6 months; QRMP quarterly filers failing for continuous 2 tax periods; composition taxpayers failing beyond 3 months from due date.
During pendency of cancellation proceedings, registration is suspended so the taxpayer is freed from routine return filing but cannot make taxable supplies.
On cancellation, the person must debit an amount equal to ITC on stock/capital goods or the output tax payable thereon, whichever is higher.
If cancelled suo-motu, the taxpayer can apply for revocation within 90 days of the cancellation order (extendible by up to 180 days by Additional/Joint Commissioner).

flow.title: Cancellation and Revocation Flow
steps: Cancellation initiated by taxpayer or proper officer
Registration suspended during inquiry
Show cause notice issued and 7-day reply given
Order of cancellation passed within 30 days
Taxpayer pays ITC or output tax on stock
Apply for revocation within 90 days if suo-motu

topics.example: A regular dealer fails to file GSTR-3B for 6 continuous months; the proper officer suspends registration, issues an SCN, and cancels registration if returns remain unfiled.
remember: Suo-motu cancellation revocation application must be filed within 90 days, extendible by another 180 days on sufficient cause.
mistakes: Believing that a taxpayer whose registration was cancelled at their own voluntary request can apply for revocation under section 30.

quiz.q: A monthly return filer becomes liable for suo-motu cancellation of registration if they fail to furnish returns for a continuous period of:
quiz.why: Rule 21(h) prescribes cancellation if a monthly return filer fails to furnish returns for a continuous period of 6 months.

quiz.q: What is the standard time limit to apply for revocation of suo-motu cancellation under section 30?
quiz.why: Section 30(1) allows a registered person to apply for revocation within 90 days from the date of service of the cancellation order.
